titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Noah's Covenant, Zion, and Canaan (ch. 9–12)
part: ch. 9–12 — Noah's Covenant, Zion, and Canaan
about: Noah dies and blesses his sons, but the devil raises up Canaan to seize Shem's kingdom; God swears to Noah that there will be no second flood and ties the rainbow to Zion, the Ark of the covenant created before the world. The Fathers affirm that the heavenly Zion prefigures Mary, and the account returns to Canaan's fall and to the line of Shem down to Terah, whose house served idols.

sentences.t: ፱ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ኪዳነ ፡ ኖሕ ።
sentences.l: 9. Concerning covenant-of Noah
sentences.i: Chapter 9: Concerning the Covenant of Noah
sentences.n: Chapter heading; ፱ = 9. በእንተ 'concerning' takes the construct state: ኪዳነ 'covenant of' (ኪዳን, with the construct ending -ä) before the name ኖሕ Noah.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ አዕረፈ ፡ ኖሕ ፡ ጻድቅ ፡ ወነግሠ ፡ ሴም ፡ በጥበብ ፡ ወበጽድቅ ፡ እስመ ፡ ተባረከ ፡ በኀበ ፡ ኖሕ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ኩን ፡ እግዚአ ፡ ለእኁከ ፤
sentences.l: And-then rested Noah (the) righteous, and-reigned Shem in-wisdom and-in-righteousness, for he-was-blessed by Noah, while he-says: 'Be lord to-your-brother';
sentences.i: After this the righteous Noah died, and Shem reigned in wisdom and righteousness, for he had been blessed by Noah, who said, 'Be lord over your brother';
sentences.n: አዕረፈ 'he rested' is the regular word for 'he died' of a righteous person. The proclitics ወ- 'and', በ- 'in', ለ- 'to/for' recur; ሴም is Shem. ተባረከ በኀበ ኖሕ 'he was blessed by Noah' (በኀበ 'by, from the side of'); እንዘ ይብል 'while saying' introduces the direct speech. ኩን እግዚአ ለእኁከ 'be lord to your brother': ኩን is the imperative of ኮነ 'be', with the predicate in the accusative (-ä). Background: Genesis 9:25–27, where Noah blesses Shem and curses Canaan; here the blessing is given the form of a charge to each son.

sentences.t: ወለካምኒ ፡ ይቤሎ ፡ ኩን ፡ ገብረ ፡ ለእኁከ ፤
sentences.l: And-to-Ham-also he-said to-him: 'Be servant to-your-brother';
sentences.i: and to Ham he said, 'Be a servant to your brother';
sentences.n: The enclitic -ኒ in ወለካምኒ is 'also, as for': 'and to Ham too'. ይቤሎ = ይቤ 'he said' + ሎ 'to him'. ገብረ 'servant' is accusative predicate after ኩን. Ham = ካም.

sentences.t: ወለያፌትኒ ፡ ይቤሎ ፡ ተገበር ፡ ወተአዛዜ ፡ ኩን ፡ ለሴም ፡ ዋርስየ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ እምድኅረ ፡ አይኅኒ ፡ ኢኀደገ ፡ ተፃርሮቶሙ ፡ ዲያብሎስ ፡ ፀርነ ፡ ለደቂቀ ፡ ኖሕ ፡ አላ ፡ አንሥኦ ፡ ለከናኦን ፡ ወልደ ፡ ካም ፡ ወኮነ ፡ መማዕልይ ፡ ዘይነፍቅ ፡ መንግሥተ ፡ እምደቂቀ ፡ ሴም ፡ እስመ ፡ ተካፈሉ ፡ ምድረ ፤
sentences.l: And-to-Japheth-also he-said to-him: 'Be-subject(?) and-obedient be to-Shem, my-heir.' And-moreover after (the) flood-also, not he-abandoned, the-devil, our-enemy, hostility-toward-them, to-sons-of Noah, but he-raised him, Canaan son-of Ham, and-he-became mighty(?), who would-seize kingdom from-sons-of Shem, for they-divided earth;
sentences.i: and to Japheth he said, 'Be subject and obedient to Shem, my heir.' Moreover, even after the flood the devil, our enemy, did not give up his hostility to the sons of Noah, but raised up Canaan, the son of Ham; and he became a powerful man who would seize the kingdom from the sons of Shem, because they had divided the earth;
sentences.n: ተገበር ወተአዛዜ 'subject and obedient' (ተገብረ, the ተ- stem of ገብረ 'to be made subject, to serve'; ተአዛዚ 'obedient', here in the accusative ተአዛዜ after ኩን). ተገበር may be the imperative ('be subject!') or a noun-like predicate before ኩን; the form is uncertain, the sense 'subject' is probable. ዋርስየ 'my heir' (ዋርስ + 1st-sing. -የ). The devil is ዲያብሎስ, 'our enemy' ፀርነ. አንሥኦ 'he raised him' (አንሥአ, the causative of the root n-s-ʾ seen in ተንሥአ 'arose', + -o 'him'). መማዕልይ is uncertain: it seems to mean 'strong, powerful (one)', but I could not confirm the form against Dillmann. ዘይነፍቅ 'who would seize' (ነፈቀ 'to take by force'); the construct መንግሥተ 'kingdom of' here stands alone as a plain accusative. The 'division of the earth' among Noah's sons is Genesis 10 (compare Jubilees 10, where Canaan settles on land that fell to Shem). ተፃርሮቶሙ 'hostility toward them' (-ሙ anticipates ለደቂቀ ኖሕ, as ለ- doubles pronoun suffixes elsewhere; 'their hostility' is the other possible reading). Names: ከናኦን Canaan.

sentences.t: ወአምሐሎሙ ፡ በስመ ፡ አምላኩ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይትዐደዉ ፡ ደወለ ፡ ቢጾሙ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ኢይብልዑ ፡ ማውታ ፡ ወብትከ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ኢይዘምዉ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይትመዐዖሙ ፡ ዳግመ ፡ በአይኅ ፡ ወኖሕኒ ፡ ተጋነየ ፡ ወሦዐ ፡ ወጸውዐ ፡ ወገዐረ ፡ ወበከየ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-adjured them by-name-of his-God that not they-transgress boundary-of their-fellows, and-that not they-eat the-dead(?) and-torn(?), and-that not they-fornicate without law, that not he-be-angry-at-them again with-flood. And-Noah-also bowed-down and-sacrificed and-called and-cried-out and-wept;
sentences.i: And he made them swear by the name of his God that they would not overstep the boundaries of their neighbours, nor eat carrion or torn flesh, nor fornicate outside the law, so that He would not be angry with them again and bring a flood. And Noah bowed down, offered sacrifice, called out, cried aloud, and wept;
sentences.n: ከመ ኢ- + subjunctive = 'that not' (negative purpose or oath-content). ደወለ ቢጾሙ 'the boundary of their fellows' (ደወል 'boundary'; ቢጽ 'companion, neighbour'). ማውታ ወብትከ I read as 'carrion and torn flesh': ማውታ is the plural of ሙት 'dead' (cf. ዕጓለ ማውታ 'orphan', literally 'child of the dead'), and ብትክ is from ብተከ 'to tear, cut in pieces'. This suits the verb 'eat' and the food rules of Genesis 9:4 and Leviticus 17:15; both words are uncertain. ይትመዐዖሙ is 'he would be angry at them'; the subject is God, unstated. Verbs of Noah's prayer: ተጋነየ 'bowed himself, did homage'; ሦዐ = ሠውዐ 'sacrificed'; ጸውዐ 'called'; ገዐረ 'cried aloud'; በከየ 'wept'. Genesis 9:8–17 is the background, but the sworn conditions here are the Kebra Nagast's own.

sentences.t: ወተናገሮ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: and-spoke-with-him God;
sentences.i: and God spoke with him.
sentences.n: ተናገሮ 'he spoke with him' (ተናገረ, reciprocal-conversational stem, + object -o).

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ ኖሕ ፡ እመሰ ፡ ዳግመ ፡ ታማስና ፡ ለምድር ፡ በአይኅ ፡ ጥስየኒ ፡ ምስሌሆሙ ፡ ለእለ ፡ ኀልቁ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አነ ፡ እትካየድ ፡ ምስሌከ ፡ ከመ ፡ ትንግሮሙ ፡ ለደቂቅከ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይብልዑ ፡ ማውታ ፡ ወብትከ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ኢይዘምዉ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ወአነሂ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢያማስና ፡ ለምድር ፡ ዳግመ ፡ በአይኅ ፡ ወከመ ፡ እሁቦሙ ፡ ለደቂቅከ ፡ ክረምተ ፡ ወሐጋየ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ወማእረረ ፡ ጸደየ ፡ ወመጸወ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-said Noah: 'If-indeed again you-destroy-her, the-earth, with-flood, destroy-me with-them who perished.' And-said-to-him God: 'I, I-will-make-a-pact with-you, that you-tell-them (to) your-sons that not they-eat the-dead(?) and-torn(?), and-that not they-fornicate without law; and-I-too, that not he-destroy-her, the-earth, again with-flood, and-that I-give-them (to) your-sons winter and-summer, seed and-harvest, spring and-autumn ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: Noah said, 'If you are to destroy the earth again with a flood, do away with me along with those who have perished.' And God said to him, 'I will make a pact with you: you shall tell your sons that they are not to eat carrion or torn flesh, nor to fornicate outside the law; and for my part I will not destroy the earth again with a flood, and I will give your sons winter and summer, seedtime and harvest, spring and autumn. . . .
sentences.n: እመሰ 'if indeed'. ጥስየኒ is read as an imperative with 'me' ('do away with me'); the verb is uncertain and the sense is inferred from the context. እትካየድ ምስሌከ 'I will make a pact with you' (ተካየደ 'to make an agreement'). ከመ + subjunctive again gives purpose or content. ታማስና and ኢያማስና are the causative አማሰነ (from መስነ 'perish') with the object suffix -ኣ 'her' (the earth), repeated by ለምድር; ኢያማስና is a 3rd-masculine form (ya-) although God speaks in the first person, as with ኢይረስዕ in chapter 10. The list of seasons answers Genesis 8:22 ('seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter'); ክረምት is the rainy season ('winter'), ሐጋይ the dry season ('summer'), ጸደይ and መጸው 'spring' and 'autumn'. The four ፨ mark the end of the chapter; the speech continues without a break into chapter 10 (God is still speaking).

sentences.t: ፲ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ጽዮን ።
sentences.l: 10. Concerning Zion
sentences.i: Chapter 10: Concerning Zion
sentences.n: Chapter heading; ፲ = 10. ጽዮን Zion is grammatically feminine in the Kebra Nagast and is the Ark (ታቦት).

sentences.t: ወእምሕል ፡ በርእስየ ፡ ወበጽዮን ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ኪዳንየ ፡ እንተ ፡ ፈጠርክዋ ፡ ለምሥሃል ፡ ወለመድኀኒተ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ወኣወርዳ ፡ በደኃሪ ፡ ለዘርእከ ፡ ወእሠምር ፡ መሥዋዕተ ፡ ደቂቅከ ፡ በዲበ ፡ ምድር ፡ ወትሄሉ ፡ ምስሌሆሙ ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ኪዳንየ ፡ ለዓለም ፡ ወሶበኒ ፡ መጽአ ፡ ደመና ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይፍርሁ ፡ ወኢይምሰሎሙ ፡ አይኅ ፡ ኣወርድ ፡ እማኅደረ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ቀስተ ፡ ኪዳንየ ፡ ዘይኬልላ ፡ ለታቦተ ፡ ሕግየ ፡ ዝውእቱ ፡ ቀስተ ፡ ደመና ፤
sentences.l: 'And-I-swear by-myself and-by-Zion, ark-of my-covenant, which I-created her for-mercy and-for-salvation-of(?) man, and-I-will-send-her-down in-the-end to-your-seed, and-I-will-be-pleased (by) sacrifice-of your-sons upon earth, and-she-will-be with-them, ark-of my-covenant, for-ever. And-whenever came cloud, that not they-fear and-not wipe-them-out(?) flood, I-will-bring-down from-dwelling-of Zion bow-of my-covenant, which encircles her, the-ark-of my-law: this-is bow-of cloud;
sentences.i: 'I swear by myself and by Zion, the Ark of my covenant, which I created for mercy and for the salvation of mankind: I will send her down at the end to your descendants, and I will accept the sacrifices of your sons upon the earth, and she will be with them, the Ark of my covenant, for ever. And whenever a cloud comes, so that they may not fear and the flood may not destroy them, I will bring down from the dwelling of Zion the bow of my covenant, which encircles the Ark of my law; this is the rainbow;
sentences.n: ወእምሕል 'and I swear'. ጽዮን ታቦተ ኪዳንየ 'Zion, the Ark of my covenant' : ታቦተ is the construct (accusative) form of ታቦት, followed by ኪዳንየ 'my covenant'. ኣወርዳ 'I will send her down' (causative of ወረደ + 'her'), recalling chapter 1 (the heavenly Zion created before the world): she comes down in the end of time (the Incarnation, see chapter 11). The wording of ምሥሃል 'mercy' and መድኀኒተ ሰብእ 'salvation (or saviour) of man' is taken as 'for mercy and for the salvation of man', which is slightly uncertain. ኢይምሰሎሙ 'it may not wipe them out': the verb is unresolved (ምሰሰ is a guess; I cannot confirm a lemma), and the sense is taken from the clause (compare Genesis 9:11, 'no more shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of a flood'). ሶበኒ 'and whenever'. Genesis 9:12–17: the bow in the cloud as sign of the covenant; here the bow comes down from Zion and surrounds the Ark (ይኬልላ, from ከለለ 'encircle'). ቀስተ ደመና 'bow of the cloud' = rainbow.

sentences.t: ወሶበኒ ፡ በዝኀ ፡ ኀጢአቶሙ ፡ ወፈቀድኩ ፡ እትመዐዖሙ ፡ እዜከራ ፡ ለታቦተ ፡ ኪዳንየ ፡ ወእሬስያ ፡ ለቀስተ ፡ ደመና ፡ ወኣአትት ፡ መዐትየ ፡ ወእፌኑ ፡ ሣህልየ ፤
sentences.l: and-whenever multiplied their-sins and-I-wish I-be-angry-at-them, I-will-remember her, the-ark-of my-covenant, and-I-will-make-her the-bow-of cloud(?), and-I-will-remove my-wrath and-send my-mercy;
sentences.i: and whenever their sins multiply and I wish to be angry with them, I will remember the Ark of my covenant and make her the rainbow, and I will put away my wrath and send my mercy;
sentences.n: እዜከራ 'I will remember her' (ዘከረ, imperfect 1st sing., with the object suffix; the verb takes the Ark as its object, with ለ marking the apposition). እሬስያ ለቀስተ ደመና: ረሰየ 'to make, set' takes two accusatives, and ለ can mark either, so 'make her the rainbow' is the likelier reading but 'set her in the rainbow' cannot be excluded; I mark it uncertain. ኣአትት 'I will remove' (a causative of a root ʾ-t-t; the root is not confirmed), contrasted with እፌኑ 'I will send'.

sentences.t: ወአንሰ ፡ ኢይረስዕ ፡ ቃልየ ፡ ወኢይሔሱ ፡ ዘወፅአ ፡ እምአፉየ ፡ ወለእመኒ ፡ ኀለፈ ፡ ሰማይ ፡ ወምድር ፡ ወቃልየሰ ፡ ኢየኀልፍ ፨
sentences.l: And-as-for-me not forget my-word nor falsify(?) that-which went-out from-my-mouth; and-if passes heaven and-earth, and-my-word-indeed not passes ፨
sentences.i: As for me, I will not forget my word nor falsify what has gone out of my mouth; even if heaven and earth pass away, my word will not pass away.
sentences.n: The verbs ኢይረስዕ and ኢይሔሱ are 3rd-person forms, in a speech where God says 'I'; the sentence reads as a statement of divine constancy ('he/I does not forget'). The sense of ኢይሔሱ is uncertain (probably 'make false, break'). Two allusions: Psalm 89:34 ('I will not alter the thing that is gone out of my lips'; 88:35 in the Greek and Latin numbering), and Matthew 24:35 ('heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away'). The suffix -ሰ in ቃልየሰ 'my word, however' marks contrast. The ፨ ends God's speech.

sentences.t: አውሥእዎ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ እለ ፡ ህየ ፡ ሊቃነ ፡ ጳጳሳት ፡ ለብፁዕ ፡ ጎርጎርዮስ ፤
sentences.l: They-answered and-said-to-him those there, chiefs-of bishops, to-the-blessed Gregory;
sentences.i: The archbishops who were there answered and said to the blessed Gregory,
sentences.n: አውሥእዎ 'they answered him' (አውሥአ + -o); ወይቤልዎ 'and they said to him'. ሊቃነ ጳጳሳት is 'chiefs of bishops', that is archbishops or senior bishops: the council assembly. ጎርጎርዮስ is Gregory, the speaker in the frame story of the Fathers' assembly (traditionally taken as Gregory the Illuminator of Armenia; the identification is not made in this text, so I leave it as uncertain). The unit introduces the Fathers' reply, which fills chapter 11.

sentences.t: ናሁኬ ፡ ይእዜ ፡ ለበውነ ፡ ጥዩቀ ፡ ከመ ፡ እምቅድመ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ፍጥረት ፡ እመኒ ፡ መላእክት ፡ ወእምቅድመ ፡ ሰማያት ፡ ወምድር ፡ ወእምቅድመ ፡ ምጽናዓት ፡ ወልጐታተ ፡ ባሕር ፡ ዘፈጠራ ፡ ለታቦተ ፡ ኪዳን ፡ ዛቲ ፡ ይእቲ ፡ እንተ ፡ በሰማያት ፡ ታንሶሱ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ምድር ፨
sentences.l: behold, now, we-have-known certainly that before all creation, even angels, and-before heavens and-earth, and-before foundations(?) and-bounds(?)-of sea, who-created her, the-ark-of covenant — this-one she, who in-the-heavens walks-about upon earth ፨
sentences.i: 'Behold, now we know for certain that before all creation, even the angels, and before the heavens and the earth, and before the foundations and the bounds of the sea, He created the Ark of the covenant: this is she who is in the heavens and walks about upon the earth.'
sentences.n: ናሁኬ 'behold, then'. ለበውነ 'we have understood' (ለበወ), ጥዩቀ 'exactly, certainly' (adverbial accusative). እምቅድመ 'before' (እም- 'from' + ቅድመ). ምጽናዓት 'foundations' is probable (cf. ጸንዐ 'be firm'), and ልጐታተ 'bounds, restraints (of the sea)' is uncertain; I could not confirm the word. ዘፈጠራ ለታቦተ ኪዳን 'who created her, the Ark of the covenant': ዘ- has no antecedent in the clause (God is understood), and the pronoun object is repeated by ለ-. እመኒ 'even, whether' is uncertain. ታንሶሱ 'she walks' (3rd fem.). The Ark is simultaneously in heaven and on earth: the foundation of the Zion-Ark theology of the book.

sentences.t: ፲፩ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ኀብሩ ፡ ፫፻፲ወ፷ ፡ ርቱዓነ ፡ ሃይማኖት ።
sentences.l: 11. To-where they-gathered 300-10-and-60 orthodox-of faith
sentences.i: Chapter 11: Where the 370 Orthodox in Faith Assembled
sentences.n: Chapter heading; ፲፩ = 11. ፫፻፲ወ፷ is 300 + 10 and 60, that is 370, as the digitized text has it. The Fathers of Nicaea number 318 (see chapter 1, ፫፻፲ወ፰); the 'sixty' ፷ is probably a slip for ፰ 'eight' (the sign shapes are close), so this may be an error in the source edition, but I render what is printed. ኀበ 'to the place where'; ኀብሩ 'they gathered'; ርቱዓነ 'orthodox of' (construct plural), ሃይማኖት 'faith'.

sentences.t: ወአውሥእዎ ፡ ወይቤሉ ፡ እወ ፡ አማን ፡ ቀደመት ፡ ተፈጥሮ ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ኪዳን ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ሐሰት ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቃልከ ፡ እሙን ፡ ወርቱዕ ፡ ወጽድቅ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ተውላጥ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-answered and-said: 'Yes, truly, she-preceded, being-created, the-ark-of covenant; and-there-is-not falsehood in-your-word. Faithful and-right and-true it-is, and-there-is-not change;
sentences.i: And they answered and said, 'Yes, truly, the Ark of the covenant was created first, and there is no falsehood in your word. It is faithful and right and true, and there is no changing it;
sentences.n: ቀደመት ተፈጥሮ 'she preceded in being created' (ቀደመ 'precede', with the infinitive ተፈጥሮ, an idiom for 'was created first'). አልቦ 'there is not'. እሙን ወርቱዕ ወጽድቅ 'faithful, right, true' : a triple of attributes. ተውላጥ 'change, exchange'.

sentences.t: አቅዲሙሰ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ፈጠራ ፡ ለማኅደረ ፡ ስብሐቲሁ ፡ ወምክረ ፡ ኪዳኑሰ ፡ ዘይቤ ፡ እለብስ ፡ ሥጋ ፡ አዳም ፡ መሬታዊተ ፡ ወኣስተርኢ ፡ ለኵሉ ፡ ዘፈጠርኩ ፡ በእዴየ ፡ ወበቃልየ ፡ ወሶበሰ ፡ ኢወረደት ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ወሶበኒ ፡ ኢለብሰ ፡ ሥጋ ፡ አዳም ፡ እመ ፡ ኢተርእየ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ቃል ፡ ወእመ ፡ ኢኮነ ፡ መድኀኒተነ ፤
sentences.l: First, for-Zion, he-created her for-dwelling-of his-glory; and-the-counsel-of his-covenant-indeed which he-said: 'I-will-put-on flesh-of Adam, earthly, and-I-will-appear to-all which I-created by-my-hand and-by-my-word'; but-if had-not descended Zion heavenly, and-if had-not he-put-on flesh-of Adam, if had-not been-seen God (the) Word, and-if had-not he-become our-saviour;
sentences.i: First, He created Zion as the dwelling of His glory; and as for the counsel of His covenant, He said, 'I will put on the flesh of Adam, earthly flesh, and I will appear to all that I created by my hand and by my word.' But if the heavenly Zion had not come down, and if He had not put on the flesh of Adam, if God the Word had not been seen and had not become our Saviour —
sentences.n: አቅዲሙሰ 'first of all'. ማኅደረ ስብሐቲሁ 'the dwelling of his glory' (chapter 1 has the same phrase with 'their glory', ማኅደረ ስብሐቲሆሙ). The quoted counsel repeats chapter 1: 'I will become man and appear to all'. መሬታዊተ 'earthly' qualifies ሥጋ (flesh). ቃል 'Word' = the Son (John 1:1, 14). The sentence breaks off after four conditions without a main clause, and it is not clear whether the Fathers mean 'then there would have been no salvation' or whether the conditions are the setting for the lesson that follows. I give the conditions as unfinished; the grammar (ሶበሰ ኢ- ... እመ ኢ-) allows either reading, so it is uncertain. ሶበ may also be read 'when' (before the Incarnation), which would make these clauses a statement of time, not of condition.

sentences.t: ስምዑ ፡ በአምሳል ፤
sentences.l: Hear by-likeness;
sentences.i: Hear by way of a likeness:
sentences.n: በአምሳል 'by a likeness, in a figure' : the speakers turn to a figurative explanation (አምሳል, as in 'image and likeness' in chapter 1).

sentences.t: ጽዮንሰ ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ተመሰለታ ፡ ለወላዲተ ፡ መድኅን ፡ ማርያም ፤
sentences.l: Zion-indeed heavenly she-resembled her, to-bearer-of saviour, Mary;
sentences.i: the heavenly Zion is likened to Mary, the bearer of the Saviour;
sentences.n: ተመሰለታ 'she was likened to her' (ተመሰለት, 3rd fem. perfect of ተመሰለ, subject Zion, + -ኣ 'her'): the suffix is doubled by ለወላዲተ, so the construction is heavy, but the sense is clear. ወላዲተ መድኅን 'bearer of the Saviour' (construct of ወላዲት 'she who bore'). The Ark as a figure of Mary is standard in Ethiopian tradition (the Ark carried the Word written on tablets; Mary the Word incarnate).

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ሕንጽት ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ወንቡር ፡ ውስቴታ ፡ ፲ ፡ ቃላት ፡ ዘሕግ ፡ እለ ፡ ጽሑፋት ፡ በእደዊሁ ፡ ወውስተ ፡ ከርሠ ፡ ማርያም ፡ ኀደረ ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ ፈጣሪ ፡ ዘበእንቲአሁ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ኮነ ፨
sentences.l: for Zion was-built, and-placed within-her ten words-of the-law, which written by-his-hands; and-within womb-of Mary dwelt he-himself, the-maker, for-whose-sake all became ፨
sentences.i: for Zion was built, and the ten words of the law were placed within her, written by His hands; and in the womb of Mary the Maker Himself dwelt, for whose sake everything came to be.
sentences.n: ሕንጽት 'built' is feminine and agrees with Zion; ንቡር 'placed' is masculine singular and stands before its plural subject ፲ ቃላት. ፲ ቃላት ዘሕግ 'ten words of the law' : the Ten Commandments (Exodus 31:18, 'written with the finger of God'; Deuteronomy 10:4). ኀደረ 'dwelt' recalls ማኅደር 'dwelling'. ዘበእንቲአሁ ኵሉ ኮነ 'for whose sake all became' echoes John 1:3 ('all things were made through him'), but በእንቲአሁ means 'for his sake, on account of him', so the match is loose. Compare chapter 8, 'for his sake they were created'.

sentences.t: ፲፪ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ከናኣን ።
sentences.l: 12. Concerning Canaan
sentences.i: Chapter 12: Concerning Canaan
sentences.n: Chapter heading; ፲፪ = 12. ከናኣን Canaan is spelled ከናኦን in chapter 9; both are the same name.

sentences.t: ወከናኣንሰ ፡ ዘነፈቀ ፡ መንግሥተ ፡ እምደቂቀ ፡ ሴም ፡ ተዐዲዎ ፡ ማሕላ ፡ ዘአበዊሁ ፡ ዘአምሐሎሙ ፡ ኖሕ ፤
sentences.l: And-Canaan-indeed, who seized kingdom from-sons-of Shem, transgressing (the) oath of-his-fathers, which Noah made-them-swear;
sentences.i: As for Canaan, he seized the kingdom from the sons of Shem by overstepping the oath of his fathers, which Noah made them swear;
sentences.n: ከናኣንሰ 'as for Canaan' (-ሰ contrast). ዘነፈቀ 'who seized' (see chapter 9). ተዐዲዎ ማሕላ 'transgressing the oath': ተዐዲዎ is a verbal noun or gerund of ተዐደወ 'to overstep'. ማሕላ 'oath' (cf. አምሐሎሙ 'he adjured them' in chapter 9). ዘአበዊሁ ዘአምሐሎሙ ኖሕ: two ዘ- in a row, the first genitival ('of his fathers'), the second a relative ('which Noah made them swear').

sentences.t: ወደቂቀ ፡ ከናኣንሰ ፡ ፯ ፡ ጽኑዓን ፡ ወነሥአ ፡ እምድረ ፡ ሴም ፡ ፯ ፡ አህጉረ ፡ ዐበይተ ፡ ወሤሞሙ ፡ ህየ ፡ ለደቂቁ ፡ ወከማሁ ፡ ካዕበ ፡ ክፍሉኒ ፡ ለርእሱ ፡ ገብረ ፤
sentences.l: And-sons-of Canaan-indeed seven (were) mighty; and-he-took from-land-of Shem seven cities great, and-he-appointed-them there, to-his-sons; and-likewise also his-portion-too for-himself he-made;
sentences.i: As for the sons of Canaan, they were seven mighty men; and he took seven great cities from the land of Shem and settled his sons there; and in the same way he also made a portion for himself;
sentences.n: ፯ = 7 (the numeral then takes the plural ጽኑዓን 'strong ones'). አህጉረ ዐበይተ 'great cities' (ሀገር 'city', pl. አህጉር; ዐቢይ 'great', pl. ዐበይት). ሤሞሙ 'he appointed or settled them' (ሠየመ). ክፍሉኒ ለርእሱ 'his own portion too for himself' : ለርእሱ 'for himself' (lit. 'for his head'). The clause is somewhat compressed, so the sense of the last phrase is a little uncertain.

sentences.t: ወበደኃሪ ፡ ተበቀሎሙ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለደቂቀ ፡ ከናኣን ፡ ወአውረሰ ፡ ምድሮሙ ፡ ለደቂቀ ፡ ሴም ፤
sentences.l: and-in-the-end took-vengeance-on-them God, on-sons-of Canaan, and-made-inherit their-lands to-sons-of Shem;
sentences.i: and in the end God took vengeance on the sons of Canaan and gave their lands to the sons of Shem as an inheritance;
sentences.n: በደኃሪ 'in the end, afterward'. ተበቀሎሙ 'took vengeance on them'. አውረሰ 'made inherit' (causative of ወረሰ 'inherit'). The reference is to the conquest of Canaan by Israel (Deuteronomy 7, Joshua), as descendants of Shem.

sentences.t: ወእሉ ፡ እለ ፡ ተዋረሱ ፡ ከናኔዎን ፡ ወፌርዜዎን ፡ ወኤዌዎን ፡ ወኬጤዎን ፡ ወኣሞሬዎን ፡ ወኢያቡሴዎን ፡ ወጌርጌሴዎን ፤
sentences.l: and-these (are those) who were-dispossessed(?): Canaanites and-Perizzites and-Hivites and-Hittites and-Amorites and-Jebusites and-Girgashites;
sentences.i: and these are the peoples who were dispossessed: the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites;
sentences.n: The seven nations of Deuteronomy 7:1 and Joshua 3:10; the Geʿez forms end in -ዎን (-ewon), the plural ending of ethnic names. ተዋረሱ is uncertain: literally 'they inherited one another' or 'were inherited', and I take it as 'were dispossessed', that is, their land was inherited by others.

sentences.t: እሉ ፡ እሙንቱ ፡ እለ ፡ ተኀየለ ፡ ከናኣን ፡ እምዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፤
sentences.l: these (are) they, who Canaan prevailed (through/over?) from-seed-of Shem;
sentences.i: these are the ones through whom Canaan grew strong at the expense of the seed of Shem;
sentences.n: ተኀየለ 'to be strong, prevail'. The grammar of እለ ተኀየለ ከናኣን እምዘርአ ሴም is uncertain: either 'those through whom Canaan became strong' (the seven peoples, his descendants) or 'those over whom Canaan prevailed'; እም- may mean 'from' or 'against'. My rendering is a compromise and should not be relied on.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ኢርቱዕ ፡ ተዐድዎ ፡ መንግሥት ፡ ወበሊዐ ፡ ማሕላ ፡ ወበእንተዝ ፡ ጠፍኡ ፡ ወዝክሮሙኒ ፡ ኀልቀ ፡ በተዐድዎ ፡ ትእዛዝ ፡ ወአምልኮ ፡ ጣዖት ፡ ወሰጊድ ፡ ለእለ ፡ ኢኮኑ ፡ አማልክተ ፨
sentences.l: for not (was) right the-transgressing (of) kingdom and-the-swallowing(?) (of) oath; and-on-account-of-this they-perished and-their-memory-too ended by-transgressing commandment and-worship-of idol and-bowing to-those who not-were gods ፨
sentences.i: for it was not right to overstep into a kingdom and to break the oath, and for this reason they perished, and their memory too came to an end, because they transgressed the commandment and worshipped idols and bowed to those who are not gods.
sentences.n: ተዐድዎ መንግሥት 'overstepping into a kingdom' (verbal noun; the final -ዎ belongs to the verbal noun, as in ተፈጥሮ). በሊዐ ማሕላ 'swallowing an oath' : I take this as the idiom for breaking an oath (lit. 'eating'), but it is a literal rendering of a metaphor and the idiom is inferred. በእንተዝ 'on account of this' (በእንተ + ዝ). ዝክሮሙ 'their memory' (compare Psalm 9:6). ሰጊድ 'bowing, worship'. ለእለ ኢኮኑ አማልክተ 'to those who were not gods' (cf. Galatians 4:8). The ፨ ends the account of Canaan; the genealogy of Shem's line follows.

sentences.t: ወእም ፡ ድኅረ ፡ ሞተ ፡ ሴም ፡ ነግሠ ፡ አልፋክስድ ፤
sentences.l: And-from after died Shem reigned Arphaxad;
sentences.i: After the death of Shem, Arphaxad reigned;
sentences.n: The line of Shem, kings in the Kebra Nagast's scheme: ሴም Shem, አልፋክስድ Arphaxad. እም ድኅረ 'after' (here written as two words; ድኅረ 'after').

sentences.t: ወእምድኅረ ፡ ሞተ ፡ አልፋክስድ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ቃይናን ፤
sentences.l: and-from-after died Arphaxad reigned Kainan;
sentences.i: after the death of Arphaxad, Kainan reigned;
sentences.n: ቃይናን Kainan (Cainan), who appears in the Septuagint of Genesis 10:24 and in Luke 3:36 but not in the Hebrew text.

sentences.t: ወእምድኅረ ፡ ሞተ ፡ ቃይናን ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ሳላ ፤
sentences.l: and-from-after died Kainan reigned Sala;
sentences.i: after the death of Kainan, Sala reigned;
sentences.n: ሳላ Sala (Shelah in the Hebrew Bible; Sala in Luke 3:35).

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ እቤር ፡ ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ፋሌቅ ፡ ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ራጋው ፡ ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ሴሮሕ ፡ ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ናኮር ፡ ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ታራ ፡ ወእሉሰ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ያሰግሉ ፡ ጣዖታተ ፡ ወየሐውሩ ፡ ኀበ ፡ መቃብረ ፡ አበዊሆሙ ፡ ወይገብሩ ፡ ሥዕለ ፡ ዘወርቅ ፡ ወብሩር ፡ ወብርት ፤
sentences.l: and-after-him reigned Eber, and-after-him reigned Peleg, and-after-him reigned Ragau, and-after-him reigned Seruh, and-after-him reigned Nahor, and-after-him reigned Terah. And-these-indeed while they-serve idols and-they-go to tomb-of their-fathers and-they-make image of-gold and-silver and-bronze;
sentences.i: after him Eber reigned, and after him Peleg, and after him Reu, and after him Serug, and after him Nahor, and after him Terah. And these kings served idols, and went to the tomb of their fathers, and made images of gold, silver, and bronze;
sentences.n: እቤር Eber, ፋሌቅ Peleg, ራጋው Reu (Ragau in Luke 3:35), ሴሮሕ Serug, ናኮር Nahor, ታራ Terah. The names follow the Septuagint-Lucan line, with Kainan included. እምድኅሬሁ 'after him' (the -ሁ suffix refers to the preceding king). ወእሉሰ 'and these, however'. ያሰግሉ 'they served' is uncertain: I cannot confirm a verb ሰገለ; the form may be a slip for ያሰግዱ (the causative of ሰገደ 'bow down', cf. ሰጊድ in chapter 12), but the sense 'served, worshipped idols' is clear. ሥዕል 'image, picture, idol'. ብርት 'bronze'. Terah's idolatry is also in Joshua 24:2.

sentences.t: ወይትናገሮሙ ፡ ጋኔን ፡ በውስተ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ሥዕለ ፡ አበዊሆሙ ፡ ወይብሎሙ ፡ እገሌ ፡ ወልድየ ፡ ሡዕ ፡ ሊተ ፡ ወልድከ ፡ ዘታፈቅር ፤
sentences.l: And-would-speak-with-them a-demon in that image of-their-fathers, and-would-say to-them: 'So-and-so my-son, sacrifice to-me your-son whom you-love';
sentences.i: and a demon would speak to them from within the image of their fathers and say to them, 'So-and-so, my son, sacrifice to me your son whom you love';
sentences.n: ወይትናገሮሙ 'and he speaks with them' : the habitual imperfect gives the sense 'would speak'. ጋኔን 'demon'. እገሌ 'so-and-so' (a placeholder for any name). ሡዕ 'sacrifice!' (imperative of ሠውዐ). ሊተ 'to me'. The phrase 'your son whom you love' is, I think, a deliberate echo of God's command to Abraham, Genesis 22:2 ('your son, your only son, whom you love'), here put into the mouth of demons.

sentences.t: ወይዘብሑ ፡ ደቂቆሙ ፡ ወአዋልዲሆሙ ፡ ለአጋንንት ፡ ወይክዕዉ ፡ ደመ ፡ ንጹሐ ፡ ለርኩሳን ፡ አጋንንት ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-they-would-sacrifice their-sons and-their-daughters to-demons, and-would-pour-out blood (that is) clean(innocent) to-unclean demons ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: and they would sacrifice their sons and their daughters to demons and shed innocent blood to unclean demons. . . .
sentences.n: ይዘብሑ 'they would sacrifice' and ይክዕዉ 'they would pour out' are habitual imperfects. ደመ ንጹሐ 'innocent blood' (ንጹሕ 'clean, innocent'). This follows Psalm 106:37–38 (105:37–38 in the Septuagint numbering): 'They sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons, and shed innocent blood.' The run of seven ፨ closes the part.
